title: Matrix-checking program semantics
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $i,dd$ natural numbers, and $\sigma$ a register state. Suppose $\sigma.n^2-i=dd$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, $\sigma.n\le |x|$, $\sigma.p=2\sigma.n+2+2i$, $\sigma.a=\lfloor i/\sigma.n\rfloor$, $\sigma.b=i\bmod\sigma.n$, and $i\le\sigma.n^2$. If the matrix-rest condition holds for $x,\sigma.n,i$, then the universal probabilistic program started at the matrix-checking site with register state obtained from $\sigma$ by setting $p=2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2+2$, $a=\sigma.n$, and $b=0$ has acceptance probability $q$. If that condition fails, then $q=0$. In either case, the program started at its multiplication-and-checking entry site with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$; the semantics also require termination along every sequence of choices and the stated register bound throughout the run.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
Conditional on the matrix-rest condition, the specified continuation has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural-number bound, $q$ a rational number, $dd,i$
natural numbers, and $\sigma$ a record of fifteen natural-number registers. Assume
$\sigma.n^2-i=dd$, each register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, $\sigma.n\le
|x|$, $\sigma.p=2\sigma.n+2+2i$, $\sigma.a=\lfloor i/\sigma.n\rfloor$,
$\sigma.b=i\bmod\sigma.n$, and $i\le\sigma.n^2$. If the bits of $x$ from position
$2\sigma.n+2+2i$ through the designated end of the matrix entries occur in equal
adjacent pairs, followed by the separator bits $01$, then the randomized program started
at its matrix-checking entry point with input $x$, bound $B$, and register record
$\sigma$ has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability $1-q$; its
corresponding run from the copy-checking point, with input pointer
$2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2+2$, row counter $\sigma.n$, and column counter $0$, has the
same semantic property. If that paired-bit and separator condition fails, then $q=0$.
